A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EMPO study and contain readable text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices. Existing content can be matched across pagination changes and the renumbering of the prompt and example appendices.

before.justification: V1 reports original EMPO training and evaluation results, component ablations, sensitivity experiments, editing-quality measurements, and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains the original empirical results and adds evaluations on additional model backbones and benchmarks in Tables 5 and 6.

M1.justification: Sections 3.2–3.3 retain the same entity-editing procedure, image/instruction/response preference objectives, entity-token weighting, and combined loss. Applying EMPO to additional backbones does not introduce a documented algorithmic modification.

E1.justification: V2 retains the original training and evaluation datasets and adds HallusionBench, MMBench, MMMU, MMVet, and MIA-Bench in Appendix C. This substantially broadens evaluation data and task coverage, including English and Chinese MMBench evaluations and additional multimodal reasoning and instruction-following tasks.

E2.justification: The original Table 1 comparator roster is retained. New Table 5 adds vanilla Muffin-13B and DPO-trained Muffin/LLaVA-NeXT controls against corresponding EMPO models. V1 included Muffin as the RLHF-V backbone, but did not report these vanilla and DPO-trained Muffin comparisons.

E3.justification: V2 adds experiments using LLaVA-NeXT-7B and Muffin-13B. Table 6 introduces benchmark-specific evaluation settings, including HallusionBench qA/fA/aA metrics, MMBench dev_en/dev_cn, and MMMU dev/test. The original experiments' stated training budgets, hyperparameters, and evaluation procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Table 5 tests whether EMPO's benefits extend across backbone architectures and scales, adding a limited generalization analysis. Existing component ablations, rejection-construction comparisons, alpha sensitivity, CLIP editing checks, the pilot error analysis, and attention examples are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures for benchmark performance. The existing CLIP similarity distributions and box plots are retained without a change in statistical reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 5–6 add substantial results. For example, newly evaluated LLaVA-NeXT-7B has CHAIRs values of 13.4, 11.9, and 5.3 for vanilla, DPO, and EMPO. Table 6 reports HallusionBench aA of 35.4 versus 48.2 and MMVet of 32.5 versus 29.7 for vanilla versus EMPO. Existing results are unchanged apart from equivalent rounding.

T1.justification: Equations 1–7 and their mathematical content remain unchanged. V2 adds no formal assumptions, propositions, proofs, or derivations; its additional explanation of DPO is conceptual.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: entity-centric three-aspect preference optimization, automatic preference-data construction, and hallucination reduction while maintaining general capabilities. The headline 85.9% and 49.8% reductions are unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 interprets the new experiments as supporting effectiveness across architectures and broader general proficiency. Appendix C incorrectly includes MMVet among consistently improved benchmarks despite Table 6 showing a decrease from 32.5 to 29.7. Existing mechanism explanations and entity-centric applicability limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A.2 adds aggregate construction costs: approximately $121 in API fees and 40 A100 hours costing about $50 through Google Colab. Appendix C identifies VLMEvalKit as the evaluation implementation. These are additional disclosures; the original hyperparameters and promised code/data release remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds references for VLMEvalKit, the additional capability benchmarks, and Muffin, plus Lyu et al. (2025) and Xu et al. (2025). The substantive positioning relative to DPO, MDPO, and earlier hallucination-mitigation approaches remains largely unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 substantially condenses the localized discussion in Appendix A.1, adds a short DPO explanation and acknowledgments, and makes grammatical corrections. New Appendix C shifts the prompt/example appendices to D/E, while the overall narrative and section organization remain stable.

P2.justification: V2 adds Tables 5 and 6, moves Tables 3–4 captions below their tables, expands Figure 1's caption, and corrects Figure 7's caption. Existing figures are retained, with limited resizing, spacing, and pagination changes within the same two-column layout.

improvement.justification: The additional backbone experiments reduce dependence on a single EMPO backbone, while broader benchmark evaluation better exposes capability tradeoffs and the cost disclosure improves practicality. These gains are tempered by Appendix C incorrectly describing the MMVet decline as an improvement. The resulting quality improvement is useful but limited.
